q: Peruvian Pisco owes as much to what it forbids as to what it allows. Give both sides.
accept: distilled to proof with no water added no wood ageing and no additives
single distillation to bottling strength cannot be diluted or barrel aged afterwards
no dilution after the still and no oak with puro acholado and mosto verde as styles
copper pot to final strength 38 to 48 percent rested in glass not wood
ans: Distilled in copper pot stills straight to its bottling strength of 38–48% abv, from eight permitted grapes, in three styles: Puro from a single variety, Acholado a blend, Mosto Verde distilled from partially fermented must. Forbidden: adding water after distillation, adding anything else at all, and any contact with wood or any vessel that would flavour it — it rests a minimum three months in glass or steel
exp: Every rule points at one idea: the distiller must land the cut exactly where the bottle will sit, so there is nowhere to hide a poor distillation. Chilean Pisco takes the opposite view — dilution and wood ageing are both permitted, Muscat dominates the plantings, and bottling strengths run lower. Mosto Verde is the luxury tier because sacrificing unfermented sugar means far more wine is consumed per bottle produced.

q: Sauternes' botrytis engine is the meeting of which two rivers?
ans: The cold Ciron meeting the warmer Garonne — morning mists, afternoon sun
exp: Multiple tries through the vineyard pick shriveled berries one by one.

q: What is a 'trie' in sweet-wine harvesting?
ans: A selective picking pass — great estates make several per season
exp: Yquem averages roughly a glass of wine per vine.

q: German BA and TBA minimum must weights sit at roughly which Oechsle bands?
exp: Eiswein shares BA's band, achieved by freeze not fungus.

q: Vin Santo's slow oxidative fermentation happens in sealed small casks called:
ans: Caratelli, under the roof through seasonal swings, with the madre starter
exp: Occhio di Pernice is the red-grape (Sangiovese-based) version — amber to mahogany, not a rosé.

accept: raisining on the vine no botrytis
ans: Passerillage — on-vine raisining in dry Pyrenean autumn wind (not botrytis)
exp: Petit Manseng's thick skins resist rot and shrivel instead.

q: Recioto di Soave earns which historical footnote?
ans: Veneto's first DOCG (1998) — dried-Garganega sweet wine
exp: 'Recie' = the ripest ear-lobes of the bunch, dried on mats.

q: Match sweet wine to concentration method.
pairs: Botrytis berries macerated in base wine
ans: Aszú–botrytis maceration · Constance–vine raisin · Eiswein–freeze · Pantelleria–dried Zibibbo
exp: Four routes, one destination: sugar beyond yeast's appetite.

q: Alsace SGN minimum must weights exceed VT by design; what does SGN stand for?
ans: Sélection de Grains Nobles — botrytized berry selection
exp: VT can be technically dry; SGN never is.

q: Moscato d'Asti finishes around what alcohol, and why?
ans: ~5.5% — fermentation is chilled and filtered to a halt, keeping sugar and fizz gentle

q: The great sweet Chenin trio of Anjou is Quarts de Chaume, Bonnezeaux and:
ans: Coteaux du Layon (with the Chaume premier cru)
exp: Layon's mists off the little river mirror Sauternes' mechanics.

q: Explain why botrytis requires humid mornings and dry afternoons specifically.
accept: moisture to infect dryness to concentrate not rot
humidity for growth dry to prevent grey rot
ans: Morning moisture lets the fungus infect; afternoon dryness concentrates the berry and prevents the infection turning to destructive grey rot
exp: Without the dry afternoon, noble rot becomes bunch rot and the crop is lost.

q: Name three botrytis-affected sweet wines outside France and Germany.
accept: tokaji aszu ruster ausbruch royal tokaji new zealand noble
ans: Tokaji Aszú (Hungary), Ruster Ausbruch (Austria), plus botrytized wines from Romania (Cotnari), Australia (De Bortoli Noble One) and New Zealand
exp: De Bortoli's Noble One is Semillon from Riverina — botrytis in an irrigated hot zone.

q: What is 'Sélection de Grains Nobles' minimum must weight relative to Vendanges Tardives?
ans: Substantially higher — roughly 276–306 g/L versus VT's 235–257, by variety
exp: Know that SGN exceeds VT and by which varieties the thresholds differ.

accept: lees starter from previous batch inoculates new wine
ans: A starter of lees from a previous batch, carried into the new caratello to inoculate and shape it
exp: Each estate's madre is a lineage — the wine's continuity across decades.

q: Which Italian sweet wine comes from the island of Pantelleria and from which grape?
ans: Passito di Pantelleria from Zibibbo (Muscat of Alexandria)
exp: Sun-dried on mats; the alberello pantesco training is UNESCO-listed.
